explicit_propositions.text: The biblical account of Jesus’ ascension is found in Luke 24:44–53 and Acts 1:3–11.
The coronavirus pandemic has caused widespread global lockdowns.
Churches have been closed to in-person worship for six or seven weeks.
Many countries are emerging from lockdown in stages, varying in pace.
Some churches have engaged in legal battles to reopen for in-person worship.
Jesus instructed his disciples to proclaim repentance and forgiveness of sins to all nations.
The speaker's church hopes to resume in-person worship on June 14th.
There is no magic in the date of June 14th; reopening depends on viral conditions.
Future worship services will emphasize health and safety measures.
The speaker believes that post-lockdown practices will persist for a long time.

assumptions.text: Scripture is authoritative and essential for interpreting Christian mission and purpose.
The spiritual significance of the ascension provides relevant guidance for current societal upheaval.
The congregation values continuity with Christian tradition despite disruption.
Discipleship requires active participation rather than passive waiting or heavenly gaze.
Repentance and forgiveness are central moral imperatives in Christian life.
The church’s role includes modeling humility, accountability, and reconciliation.
Social healing and unity are achievable through shared Christian witness.
The Holy Spirit empowers believers to carry out mission effectively.
Congregants are capable and responsible agents of change in their communities.
The metaphor of stagecoach tickets implies equal moral obligation among all members of the church.
